backend: WebNN via Core ML, deviceType gpu (MLComputeUnitsAll)

protocol.abProtocol: For deltas: N complete configurations built in ONE page session, all graphs resident, timed interleaved A,B,A,B in two blocks of 20-50. A difference counts only if it exceeds 1 ms in BOTH blocks, and every claimed win needs a byte-identical position control in the last slot, because slot bias alone reaches +-1.4 ms.
protocol.coldStart: out of scope; Chromium has no compiled-graph cache

newPrompt.note: tokenize -> text graph -> image graph -> readback -> ImageData -> putImageData, quiet machine

cachedPrompt.note: same prompt again: the embedding MLTensor still holds it, so the text graph is not dispatched at all

ortWebGPU.runtime: ONNX Runtime Web, WebGPU EP, Microsoft's SD-Turbo demo

ortWebNN.runtime: ONNX Runtime Web, WebNN EP via Core ML, same demo

nativeMPS.runtime: Native PyTorch MPS, diffusers, float16 + TAESD

baselines.comparabilityNote: The two ORT rows use the demo's full VAE; ours and the native row use TAESD. The VAE decode column is therefore not like for like; the total is, in the sense that it is what a user waits for.

history.note: pass four measured two levers and changed no default

todo-2-nearest-64.what: Token Downsampling: the K/V of the five 64x64 attn1 layers are nearest-subsampled 2x, pooled BEFORE to_k/to_v so the projections shrink too. The float16 score tensor goes 168 MB -> 42 MB.

quality.reading: Composition, colour and subject are preserved; fine detail is re-rolled (thin rims, whiskers). This is not a lossless optimisation: it is a slightly different image for 20% less time.

avgPoolingIsWorse.note: nearest beats avg on every prompt and every metric

todo-2-nearest-64.caveat: One octave more aggressive than anything the ToDo paper measured: they use factor 2 at 1024x1024 / 16,384 tokens; this is factor 2 on a 4,096-token grid.

fused-sdpa-upstream.status: not available in any browser; measured natively as the upstream case
fused-sdpa-upstream.what: All 32 matmul-softmax-matmul triples replaced with a single ios18.scaled_dot_product_attention in the MIL translation.
fused-sdpa-upstream.quality: MORE accurate: 45.53 dB vs 44.82 dB, because the float16 score tensor is never materialised
fused-sdpa-upstream.blocker: Chromium exposes no scaledDotProductAttention in the WebNN surface, and the MIL op lacks the `scale` argument this graph needs (cancelled with a mul today).
fused-sdpa-upstream.projection: With such an op the exact graph would be about 52 ms and more accurate than it is now.

floor.reasoning: conv and matmul are at hardware efficiency (678 GFLOPs at ~12 TFLOP/s against a measured float16 vector peak near 13); the softmaxes cannot be spelled cheaper at WebNN level because Chromium exposes no fused attention op, so the [5,4096,4096] scores are materialised; and every cheap category has been measured, not modelled, at approximately zero. Getting under 60 needs a new op in the WebNN surface or fewer FLOPs, not another graph rewrite.

measurementCaveat: Pass-three sessions 3-5 and all of pass four ran with an unrelated compute job on the machine (load 15-20). Interleaved deltas are immune, since both arms share the load; absolute readings from those sessions are 1-5 ms pessimistic. The 67.85 ms headline is from the quiet-machine sub-pixel session.

reproducedByLoader.note: scripts/verify.mjs replaying these recipes through runtime/loader.js, on the same machine the originals were measured on. The machine was carrying an unrelated compute job throughout (load average 16 to 18, an ORCA SCF run plus a VM), so absolutes are 0 to 5 ms pessimistic; the workbench documented the same effect.
reproducedByLoader.determinism: All three builds produced the same 1,048,576-byte RGBA readback, byte for byte, across both constant-loading paths.

loaderCost.note: emitMs is the replay itself: 2 to 8 ms for 1441 ops, against the 3,569 ms the original emitter spent building the same graph. buildMs is Core ML compiling, and Chromium caches none of it.
